name: Non-syndromic Urogenital Tract Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Urogenital Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural abnormalities of the urogenital tract without associated syndromic features
Exclusion of syndromic or chromosomal abnormalities by clinical and genetic evaluation
Confirmation of malformation by imaging modalities such as ultrasound, voiding cystourethrogram, or MRI
Positive family history of isolated urogenital malformations (supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital urogenital tract malformation confirmed by imaging with exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, radiological, and genetic assessments.

laboratory: Urinalysis showing recurrent infections or hematuria
Renal function tests typically normal unless secondary damage
imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating structural anomalies of kidneys, ureters, or bladder
Voiding cystourethrogram showing vesicoureteral reflux or urethral abnormalities
MRI pelvis for detailed soft tissue and anatomical assessment
genetic: No consistent pathogenic variants identified; genetic testing used to exclude syndromic causes
other: Physical examination revealing external genital malformations such as hypospadias or chordee

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of additional systemic or syndromic features
Obstructive membrane in posterior urethra diagnosed by voiding cystourethrogram
Typically presents with bladder outlet obstruction and renal impairment

redFlags: Severe obstructive uropathy with bladder dysfunction
